comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I’m Param, one of the founders of Versine.AI agents can already research, book, plan and buy things for us. But ask one to pay your friend back for dinner and it hands the job right back to you. Banks were built for humans tapping through screens, so the moment money has to move between people, your agent hits a wall.Versine lets your AI send and request money through an MCP. Tell ChatGPT, Claude, or your own agent “send Nate $25 for dinner” and it sets up the payment. You approve it with your passkey and the money’s on its way.What you can do:Pay or request money from up to 100 people in one prompt. Splitting a trip or a group dinner takes one message.Pay anyone, even if they’re not on Versine. They cash out to their bank in minutes.Stay in control. Your AI sets up payments, but nothing moves until you approve it with your passkey.Skip approval when you want to (optional). Auto-approve small payments to people you trust, within limits you set.Your funds are held entirely by you, signed by your passkey. No one else in the world, including Versine, or your agent can ever have direct access without your approval. All financial transactions are handled by licensed partners. Your AI never sees your bank credentials.The Versine mobile iPhone and Android apps are where you approve payments and manage your account. Paying anyone with Versine is completely free. The only fee is on instant FedNow withdrawals to your bank, and we pass that cost through with no markup.We started building this after seeing a contradiction: assistants were meant to be useful for people but when it came to finance and money movement, they were frustratingly hands off. We realized that if people could send money just by talking to ChatGPT or Claude, that bottleneck would disappear.We’d love your feedback, especially on this: what’s the first thing you’d want your AI to pay for? comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋Like most people I'd got into the habit of hitting "Accept all" on every cookie banner just to get to the page (the reject button is usually there, it's just been made a lot more work). week.name: Filament by Galaxy
week.tagline: Move data using your terminal or agent. Fast & open source.
week.description: Filament is a data replication engine written in Go. It supports full loads, incremental replication, and change data capture (CDC). As data moves through the engine, Filament verifies Arrow batches at the sink handoff and, where the sink supports it, checks the exact serialized payload. You can run Filament as a standalone binary or embed it in a Go application.

comments.text: The combination of CDC, incremental replication, and batch verification is interesting. How does Filament handle recovery after a destination outage, especially when the source continues receiving writes during downtime?

Checksumming the Arrow batch and recomputing it at the sink is a good answer to the quiet failure in pipelines, where rows arrive but not quite as they left. Advancing checkpoints only after the destination commits makes replays safer too. How do you handle a schema change mid CDC stream, like a column type change on the source, without breaking verification or forcing a full reload?

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt,I'm Ravi, co-founder of Scalekit. Today we're launching AgentKit, an MCP gateway that handles auth and tool-calling for AI agents in production.Why now? Over the last year, wiring an agent to a tool got easy. MCP standardized the interface, and any agent can now call Gmail or Salesforce after an afternoon of work.But the tool call is only the surface. Once an agent ships to real users, everything underneath it shows up:whose credentials each call executes withwhich tools each agent should have in contextthe internal systems no catalog coverswhat happens when an upstream API pushes backwho's accountable for every actionThat layer decides whether an agent makes it to production. It's what we built AgentKit for.Try it free: scalekit.com. The free tier includes 10,000 tool calls a month and all 600+ connectors. Make your first tool call from the dashboard, or start from your terminal with npx @ scalekit-inc/cli setup.Here's what it looks like in practice.Say you're shipping a sales agent inside your product. A rep types: "Prep me for the Acme renewal. Pull the deal, the last three email threads, what the team said in Slack, when we last met them, and how much they've used the product this quarter."Four apps, one ask. Getting it working for one rep in a demo is easy. Here's what's underneath when it runs for every rep at every customer:Thousands of OAuth grants, not four. 40 customers × 30 reps × Salesforce, Gmail, Slack and Calendar = 4,800 connected accounts. Each needs its tokens stored, isolated per customer, and refreshed before they expire mid-run. → AgentKit manages connected accounts end to end. Users authorize through an auth link you surface in your app. Tokens live in a per-tenant AES-256 vault, refresh automatically, and are injected at execution time. They never touch your code, logs, or prompts.Every call has to execute as the right user. The agent should see what that rep can see at that customer, and nothing more. Not a shared service account with org-wide access to every inbox. → Every tool call executes with the end user's own credentials, within the scopes they granted.Every tool definition costs context. Gmail alone exposes ~30 tools; four apps put over a hundred on the table. At ~200 tokens per definition, 40 tools burn ~8,000 tokens before the agent does any work, and tool selection gets worse as the list grows. Your prep agent needs about ten tools. Your outbound agent needs a different ten. → Virtual MCP Servers let you compose a tool set per agent role, across connectors. Each role gets one static MCP URL; you mint a short-lived session token per user per run. Smaller context and least-privilege access: ten tool definitions (~2,000 tokens) instead of over a hundred (20,000+).The data you need has no connector. Usage lives in your customer's internal analytics service. No catalog covers it, so you'd build that integration yourself, auth included. → Define it as a custom connector (OAuth 2.0, API key, bearer token, RSA or basic auth), or point AgentKit at a remote MCP server. It runs on the same gateway with the same credential handling and logs as the 600+ built-in connectors.It has to hold up and be auditable. Rate limits, timeouts, upstream errors the model can't act on. Then a deal stage changes and someone asks whether the rep did it or the agent did. → Retries and rate limits are handled on every call. Every call is logged with agent, user, tool and response, and logs stream to Datadog or Splunk.None of this shows up in a demo. All of it shows up in production. AgentKit handles that layer: 30,000+ tools across 600+ apps behind one MCP gateway. And with Triggers, an agent can start on its own the moment an email lands.Python and Node SDKs. Works with the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, Google ADK, Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, and Claude Code. You keep your framework and backend.Which of these five has slowed your agent down the most?

So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 Joel here, one of the two Swedish founders building Goldfish.Why we built it:We started building Goldfish because AI still has one weird problem: it knows the internet, but not the work sitting right in front of you. AI has memory like a goldfish!Your messages, docs, tabs, meetings, half-written drafts, people, decisions, and loose threads already live on your computer. But every time you open a chatbot, you start from zero again. You paste the thread, explain the project, describe the person, and try to make it sound like you.That felt backwards to us.What Goldfish is:Goldfish is a private AI memory layer for your Mac. It understands what you’re working on across apps, then lets you use that context anywhere you type.Press ⌥ Option in any text field and Goldfish can help you:write replies in your own tone, with the thread and relationship context already theresummarize messy work from Slack, Gmail, docs, tabs, or meetingsrecall things you saw, wrote, read, or discussedrewrite highlighted text without touching the restbring your full computer context into Claude Desktop through our local MCP serverWhat we believe:The best AI product won’t be another empty chat box.It will be the memory layer underneath your work. Something that understands your context privately, shows up where you already are, and removes the need to re-explain yourself 50 times a day.Early traction:We’ve worked closely with 1,000+ founding members to build a product people can’t live without. GTM people at ElevenLabs, Deel, and Vercel are already using Goldfish to write faster replies in their own tone.Our founding team comes from Strawberry Browser (General Catalyst) and Depict (YC20), and we’re currently building from The Bridge by Entrepreneur First in San Francisco.Privacy:Privacy is core to the product. Your memory stays on your Mac in a local database. No cloud sync, no backend where we can browse your data, and you can stop capture of apps and domains any time. AI calls have zero data retention.Product Hunt offer:Goldfish is still in closed beta, but we’re opening early access to the Product Hunt community first.As a thank you, everyone from Product Hunt gets 3 months of free access!!
